beliefs: f inserts '2' at index len//2 of the input [E1, E2]
After insertion, if the last character is an ASCII letter, it is shifted forward by 2 in ASCII (a->c, z->b wrapping, A->C, Z->B wrapping) [E1, E2, E3]
The shift wraps around within the alphabet: 'z'->'b' and 'Z'->'B' rather than going past 'z'/'Z' [E3]
Non-letter last characters (digits, symbols, spaces) are left unchanged [E1, E3]
Only the last character is shifted, not every letter [E3]
Empty input returns '2' (insertion still happens at index 0, no letter to shift) [E4]
notes: E4 shows empty input yields '2', not '', so the insertion applies even to empty strings; removed the empty-string special case.
